toolSpecificData.result:
No security vulnerabilities found in the reviewed changes.

Checked `DiscussionDtos`, discussion and admin controllers, authentication and security configuration, account and discussion services, entities, repositories, and exception handling. Public registration assigns `STUDENT`; admin provisioning is restricted to `ADMIN`; moderation requires `FACULTY` or `ADMIN`; post/comment edits and deletes check authorship or admin status. Queries use Spring Data repository methods, with no SQL construction found.

Limit: the Java app returns user content as JSON or plain text, and I found no renderer in `functional-codebase`; I can’t assess whether an external client later renders that content unsafely. The DTO file was reviewed as requested but is not changed in the working tree; the Java diff is limited to a formatting-only change in `SecurityConfiguration.java`.

toolSpecificData.result:
## Reassessment: no confirmed stored XSS

The evidence confirms that script-looking text can be accepted, persisted, and returned by the API—but not that it executes in a browser.

- **Input and persistence:** `PostRequest.body` allows a string up to 100,000 characters, with no HTML sanitization: `C:\Users\wildm\Documents\Projects\cs763-wildman-final-project\cs763-wildman-final-project\functional-codebase\src\main\java\edu\bu\met\wildmancs763\discussions\api\DiscussionDtos.java:20-23`. `DiscussionService` trims the body, saves the post, and maps the stored value into the response: `...\service\DiscussionService.java:45-49, 233, 330-337`. The entity persists it as a `@Lob` string: `...\domain\DiscussionPost.java:35-37`.
- **API response:** The controller is a `@RestController` and returns `PostResponse` objects; create, list, get, update, and timeline paths use that response model: `...\api\DiscussionController.java:35, 45-54, 57-77, 79-91, 96-114`. The project includes Spring MVC and Jackson (`...\functional-codebase\pom.xml:48, 52`). Returning `<script>alert(1)</script>` as a JSON string is not, by itself, HTML execution; the observed 200 response does not demonstrate XSS.
- **Rendering sinks and CSP:** The tracked repository contains no browser client, HTML template, or client-side source that renders the post body. A repository search found no relevant HTML/Markdown rendering or unsafe DOM sink. `SecurityConfiguration.java:46-69` does not explicitly configure a CSP; that absence does not make this JSON response executable or establish XSS.

**Scope limit:** This conclusion covers the code in this repository. A separate client not present here could create stored XSS if it inserts the returned body into an HTML/DOM sink without escaping.

**Conditional remediation:** For plain-text posts, render the value using framework-escaped interpolation or `textContent`, not `innerHTML`. If rich HTML or Markdown is intended, sanitize the rendered HTML with a strict allowlist before inserting it into the DOM. A restrictive CSP is useful defense-in-depth, not a substitute for safe rendering. JSON serialization alone is not protection if a client later treats the value as HTML.

 # Research Blog & Project Discussion Board
 
 Spring Boot REST service for scoped academic announcements, project update posts, nested comments, moderation, search, and timeline reads.
 
 ## Run and test
 
 From the repository root:
 
 ```powershell
 .\mvnw.cmd -f functional-codebase\pom.xml spring-boot:run
 .\mvnw.cmd -f functional-codebase\pom.xml test
 ```
 
 The service listens on port `8080` and uses an in-memory H2 database. To build and run the container with `functional-codebase` as the build context:
 
 ```powershell
 docker build -t research-discussion-board functional-codebase
 docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 research-discussion-board
 ```
 
 ## API
 
 All routes are under `/api/v1/discussions`.
 
 | Method | Route | Purpose |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | `POST`, `GET` | `/posts` | Create/list posts; list supports `keyword`, `projectId`, `courseId`, `labId`, `category`, `authorHandle`, `from`, and `to`. |
 | `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | `/posts/{postId}` | Read, replace, or delete a post. |
 | `GET` | `/scopes/{projects\|courses\|labs}/{scopeId}/timeline` | Read a chronological scoped timeline; accepts `keyword`, `category`, `from`, and `to`. |
 | `POST`, `GET` | `/posts/{postId}/comments` | Create/list nested comments; listing supports `keyword`, `authorHandle`, `from`, and `to`. Use `?format=text` to download a text manifest. |
 | `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | `/posts/{postId}/comments/{commentId}` | Read, edit, or delete a comment. |
 | `PATCH` | `/posts/{postId}/moderation` | Set a post status to `active`, `reported`, or `hidden_by_moderator`. |
 | `PATCH` | `/posts/{postId}/comments/{commentId}/moderation` | Set a comment moderation status. |
 
 Post categories are `ACADEMIC_ANNOUNCEMENT` and `PROJECT_UPDATE_BLOG`. A post request must provide exactly one of `projectId`, `courseId`, or `labId`. Comment requests use `message`, `authorHandle`, and an optional `parentCommentId`. Hiding a post hides its comment stream; hiding a comment also hides its recursive replies.
 
 The specification does not define an authentication or faculty identity provider. Moderation routes currently perform status management without role authorization and must be protected by the institution's authentication layer before public deployment.

 # User accounts and discussion API
 
 The API supports local accounts and session-based login. Public registration creates a `STUDENT` account; only an administrator can provision `FACULTY` or `ADMIN` accounts. Posts and comments use the authenticated username as their author, so client-supplied author handles are ignored.
 
 ## Getting a session
 
 State-changing requests require both the `JSESSIONID` session cookie and a CSRF token. Start by requesting `GET /api/v1/auth/csrf`, retaining the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and the `token` in the response. Send the cookie and token in the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header when calling `POST /api/v1/auth/register` with a username and password (at least 12 characters). Then request a fresh CSRF token and call `POST /api/v1/auth/login` with the same credentials. Retain the session cookie returned by login; fetch a fresh CSRF token after login and include it on subsequent `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` requests.
 
 `GET /api/v1/auth/me` returns the signed-in account, and `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` ends the session. Discussion reads remain public. Authenticated users can create content and edit or delete their own content; administrators can manage any content. Faculty and administrators can use the existing moderation endpoints. User provisioning is available at `POST /api/v1/admin/users` to administrators.
 
 ## Initial administrator and persistence
 
 Configure both `APP_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME` and `APP_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` before starting the service to create the initial administrator. Use a unique, strong password and keep it in a deployment secret store; do not commit it. The bootstrap account is created only when it does not already exist. If the configured name belongs to a non-admin account, startup fails rather than silently elevating it.
 
 By default, the service persists H2 data under `./data/discussions`. In Docker, mount a durable volume at `/app/data`. `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USERNAME`, and `DATABASE_PASSWORD` can configure an alternate datasource when its JDBC driver is included in the application. Deploy behind HTTPS and set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true` in production.
